feedback.problem:
A man stocked a pond with $250$ fish. After $t$ weeks, the number of fish in the pond is given by the function 

$$
F(t)=250+{\int }_{0}^{t}(8x-24)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time (in weeks) since the man put the fish in the pond.

At what time is the number of fish in the pond at a minimum, and how many fish are there at that time?
feedback.worked_solution:
To find when the number of fish in the pond is at minimum, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}F}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}F}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(250+{\int }_{0}^{t}(8x-24)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(250)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({\int }_{0}^{t}(8x-24)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(8x-24)\,\text{d}x \\  & =8t-24\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}F}{\text{d}t}=0$:

$$
8t-24=0\,⟹\,t=3
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=3.$ To find out how many fish are when $t=3,$ we figure out $F(3)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}F(3) & =250+{\int }_{0}^{3}(8x-24)\,\text{d}x \\  & =250{[4{x}^{2}-24x]|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =250+[(4(3)^{2}-24(3))-(0)] \\  & =250-36 \\  & =214\end{aligned}
$$

Since $214<250$, we conclude that the minimum number of fish in the pond is $214$, and this will happen after $3$ weeks.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: The minimum is $214$ fish after $3$ weeks
